chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Al-Nadr ibn Suwayd, from Hisham ibn Salim, from Suleyman ibn Khalid, who said:

I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about a man whose tail bone was broken, so he lost control of his excretion, so what is due regarding it from the wergild? He (peace be upon him) said: 'The complete wergild.'

He (the narrator) said, 'And I asked him (peace be upon him) about a man who copulated with a slave girl, so he was rough with her, and when she came down from that situation, she could no longer give birth. He (peace be upon him) said: 'The complete wergild'.'

key_terms.أَفْضَاهَا: He was rough with her / copulated with her

ai.seo_question: What injuries obligate the complete wergild (diyah) according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) establishes that both the loss of excretion control due to a broken coccyx and infertility in a slave girl from rough intercourse necessitate the full wergild (diyah). This ruling highlights the Shia jurisprudential principle that specific functional impairments, whether physiological or reproductive, are valued equally to major bodily injuries in terms of compensation. The hadith underscores the comprehensive nature of diyah calculations, ensuring that non-fatal but life-altering damages receive equitable redress.

en.hubeali: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Al Husayn Bin Saeed, from Al Nazar Bin Suweyd, from Hisham Bin Salim, from Suleyman Bin Khalid who said,

‘I asked Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> about a man who broke his tail bone (coccyx), so he lost control of his excretion, so what was with regards to it from the wergild. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘The complete wergild’.

He (the narrator) said, ‘And I asked him<sup>asws</sup> about a man who copulated with a slave girl, so he was rough with her, and when she came down from that situation, she could no longer give birth. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘The complete wergild’.
